notes: Eclipse Loop 2.1.0 Your licence is a file now Activation used to work by reading your machine's hardware ID, signing it, and tying the key to that one computer. It worked, but it made the licence a property of the machine instead of a property of the purchase — and that has a cost you only feel later. New laptop, replaced logic board, reinstalled macOS: the key that was yours stopped being yours, and the only fix was to come back and ask for another one. A licence is now a signed file. You get YourName.eclipselicense when you buy. Open Eclipse Loop, choose Activate → Choose Licence File…, pick it, and the title bar reads Licensed to <your name. Keep the file somewhere you keep things — it is yours, it does not expire, and it works on the machines you own. What that changes for you - No hardware binding. Move to a new Mac, or a PC, and bring the same file. - No network check. Activation is a signature test against a public key compiled into the app. Eclipse Loop does not phone home to validate your licence — there is no server to be down, no request to be logged, and nothing about your machine leaves it.
